_comment: Every distinct Numbers question, with a hash of the prompt, the answer and the distractors that were read. A question whose hash no longer matches has changed since its last reading and must be read again. Generated by scripts/build-numbers-question-ledger.mjs; the decisions are written by the person reading.

num-lesson-age/listen_choose/num-age-hon.why: Read again after the listening pool started preferring taught words of the same role. It was drawing 영, 공 and 영하 — three ways of saying zero — into questions about counting words, and a learner who did not hear the clip could still reason about which button the lesson wanted. The options are now other counting words.

num-lesson-age/listen_choose/num-age-q.why: 몇 살이에요? was the only whole question in its lesson, so a clip of it stood against single syllables and was findable by length. The lesson now teaches the three registers — 몇 살이에요?, 나이가 어떻게 되세요?, 연세가 어떻게 되세요? — and they are asked against each other.

num-lesson-age/read_choose/num-age-honor.why: The honorific gloss was the only lower-case option in the list, which is a formatting tell on the one question it is the answer to. Capitalised to match its siblings.

num-lesson-age/read_choose/num-age-neutr.why: The three ways of asking an age were glossed *the phrase for asking someone's age*, *the everyday polite way to ask an adult's age* and *the polite way to ask an older person's age*. The first is true of all three and the other two both say polite; in Thai and Telugu two of them read as the same sentence. Each now names who you say it to — a friend, an adult you have just met, someone much older — which is what the lesson teaches.

num-lesson-dates/listen_choose/num-d-jun.why: The answer is the only two-syllable option: 유월 against 육, 오 and 칠. Kept, because the distractors are exactly what a learner reaching for June wrongly says, and the syllable count is a weak tell in a question whose whole content is a sound. Recorded rather than fixed, so the next pass starts from a reading and not from silence.

num-lesson-minutes/listen_choose/num-t-m.why: As screenshot 2 for 세 시 삼십 분. Its gloss also read "an hour and minutes together" — a description of a form standing among times — and is now 3시 30분.

num-lesson-minutes/listen_choose/num-t-q.why: Screenshot 2. A clip of 두 시 십오 분 offered against 분 and 초 — two complete times among two bare unit words. Every option is a complete hour-and-minute time now, and two more were written so there are four.

num-lesson-mixed/read_choose/num-ch-mone.why: Screenshot 3. 오천 원 asked against 2시, 사람 세 명 and 30분 — the only option about money. Now four money amounts, under 얼마를 뜻할까요? rather than 무슨 뜻일까요?.

num-lesson-money/read_choose/num-m-10000.why: Same list as screenshot 1 seen from the other side: 만 원 stood against a definition. All four options are amounts now.

num-lesson-money/read_choose/num-m-35000.why: As above for 삼만 오천 원.

num-lesson-money/read_choose/num-m-5000.why: The three prices had no gloss, so `meaningOf` rendered them as bare numerals and this list was one prose option among three numbers — the answer was pickable by shape. The prices now carry a gloss, so every option is prose.

num-lesson-money/read_choose/num-m-won.why: Screenshot 1. The answer 한국 돈의 단위 stood against 5,000원, 10,000원 and 35,000원 — a definition among three amounts, findable by shape. 원 now declares domain `definition` and is asked against other units the learner has already met.

num-lesson-ordinals/choose_system/num-o-.why: Every ordinal in Korean takes the native set, so all nine of this lesson's *which set?* questions have the same answer and a learner could tap 고유어식 without reading. Kept: it is the rule the lesson exists to teach, it is the one question shape a learner who cannot hear has beside the meaning question, and the discrimination it looks thin on is made where it bites — 이 번째 is on the screen in counter_form and is the answer in spot_mistake.
